data.title: Show HN: Undetectag, track stolen items with AirTag
data.author: pompidoo
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个可以让AirTag变为更难被小偷发现的小工具——"Undetectag"。使用这个附加装置，可以大大降低AirTag被小偷偷走并移除的可能性，概率减少95%。它适用于保护汽车、船只、自行车、摩托车、行李和背包等贵重物品。文章还提供了一个联系表单，用户可以通过填写姓名、电子邮件、电话号码和留言来获取更多信息或提出问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AirTag定制化与跟踪功能的改进及相关问题

不同观点：
• **定制化功能的建议**：
  - [gojomo] 提出多种定制化功能，如只有在没有其他AirTag存在时才启动、具备运动传感器、内置时钟和随机化种子、以及低功耗接收器等。
  - [stavros] 建议添加加速度计，仅在设备完全停止移动后激活，减少“跟踪”提示的可能性。
  
• **现有解决方案的提及**：
  - [RomanPushkin] 指出Tile已有类似功能，但需要验证，且若用于跟踪将面临高额罚款。
  
• **微控制器的选择**：
  - [ale42] 质疑使用STM32微控制器的必要性，建议使用更便宜、省电的PIC10系列微控制器。
  
• **跟踪可靠性的讨论**：
  - [pimlottc] 担心定制化功能（如静止时激活）会降低跟踪的可靠性，特别是在没有Find My网络设备的农村地区。
  
• **防止小偷发现和破坏**：
  - [econ] 建议添加一个普通标签，让小偷可以找到，但实际AirTag可能隐藏。
  - [wepple] 提出使用两个交替供电的AirTag来绕过苹果的检测，同时提供位置信息，但也担心苹果可能通过更新固件来阻止这种方法。

• **便宜仿制品的支持**：
  - [Gys] 建议支持更便宜的仿制品，因为它们不会更新固件，并提议提供包含这种跟踪器的套餐。

• **产品可靠性和保障**：
  - [turtlebits] 质疑产品的可靠性，对95%的找回率表示怀疑，并询问如果物品被找到但AirTag被移除的情况是否有补偿。

• **对产品合法性和限制的批评**：
  - [anonymousiam] 批评AirTag的限制是由于不必要的规定，认为这些限制影响了追踪被盗物品的实用性，并质疑为何不销售不公开提示的标签。

• **时间间隔的可调整性**：
  - [cinntaile] 询问时间间隔是否可由用户调整或硬编码，以及调整的限制是什么。

• **市场产品设计的动机**：
  - [Gibbon1] 引用业内人士观点，认为当前市场更倾向于销售位置数据，而不是开发长效、非持续传输的定位设备。

补充讨论：
- 评论中涉及多个技术细节的讨论，如微控制器的选择和定制功能的实现。
- 存在对苹果固件更新可能阻止某些定制功能实现的担忧。
- 争议的焦点包括AirTag功能限制的合理性及市场产品的设计动机。

data.title: Tek – A music making program for 24-bit Unicode terminals
data.author: smartmic
data.article_summary: Tek是一个用于Linux终端的音乐制作程序，采用Rust编写，基于ratatui和crossterm，支持JACK和Pipewire。它提供24位Unicode终端支持，具备编曲、播放/暂停、删除音符等功能，并推荐使用MIDI控制器和LV2插件。Tek的设计目标包括支持重采样（即播放时录制）、低资源消耗、以及便于脚本编写和映射的简洁项目格式。用户可以通过下载二进制文件或从源代码构建来安装Tek，Arch Linux用户可通过AUR获取。该程序受跟踪器和硬件音序器启发，适合在后台运行以记录音乐灵感。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：终端中的音乐制作工具和演示视频的反馈与技术问题

不同观点：
• [tzmlab] 分享了一个演示视频链接，展示了某个基于终端的音乐制作工具。
• [__m] 希望看到一个基于跟踪器的工具，认为那更适合在终端中使用。
• [neilv] 澄清该工具似乎不涉及Tek终端图形，并猜测名字可能是致敬。
• [chaosprint] 推荐了另一个基于终端的音乐制作工具Glicol-CLI，适合喜欢直接用代码创作音乐的人。
• [Sharlin] 对UI中的轴向设计有不同看法，提到更喜欢过去将通道放在x轴、时间放在y轴的做法。
• [stuaxo] 表达了对24位Unicode终端硬件的期望，似乎对当前工具的显示效果有所期待。
• [MarcelOlsz] 赞赏顶视的跟踪器UI，并分享了Aphex Twin和Hitori Tori使用类似工具的视频，认为这些视频非常震撼。
• [montag] 对UI表示赞赏，并询问是否有YouTube的快速演示视频。
• [cocodill] 提到二进制文件有问题，输出的错误信息非常 cryptic。
• [yahoozoo] 询问是否有支持VIM键绑定的数字音频工作站（DAWs）。
• [RIMR] 指出构建脚本中的一个拼写错误，提醒不要使用`bin/`，而应使用`build/`。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户对工具的UI设计和功能实现提出了个人偏好和建议。
• 技术问题如二进制文件错误和构建脚本拼写错误成为讨论的一部分。
• 一些用户分享了相关的资源和视频链接，以供其他用户参考。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在工具的UI设计和终端适用性上，部分用户对UI的轴向设计有不同看法。
• 另外，工具的二进制文件问题也引发了一些技术性讨论。

README.md
tek
a music making program for
24-bit unicode terminals
.
written in
rust
with
ratatui
on
crossterm
for
jack
and
pipewire
.
tek
is available as
source
,
statically linked binaries
, and on the
aur
.
author is reachable via
mastodon
@unspeaker@mastodon.social
or
matrix
@unspeaker:matrix.org
usage
requirements:
linux; jack or pipewire; 24-bit terminal (i use
kitty
)
recommended:
midi controller; samples in wav format; lv2 plugins.
keymaps
Arranger:
arrows: navigate
tab: enter editor
q
: enqueue clip
space: play/pause
Editor:
arrows: navigate
,
/
.
: change note length
enter: write note
-
/
=
: zoom midi editor
z
: zoom lock/unlock
del: delete
Global:
esc: options menu
f1: help/command list
f2: rename
f6: save
f9: load
installation
binary download
you can download
tek 0.2.0 "almost static"
from codeberg releases. this standalone binary release, should work on any glibc-based system.
from distro repositories
arch linux
tek 0.2.0-rc7
is available as a package in the AUR.
you can install it using your preferred AUR helper (e.g.
paru
):
paru -S tek
building from source
requires docker.
git clone --recursive -b 0.2 https://codeberg.org/unspeaker/tek
cd tek                             # enter directory
cat bin/release-glibc.sh           # preview build script
sudo bin/release-glibc.sh          # run build script
sudo cp bin/tek /usr/local/bin/tek # install
design goals
inspired by trackers and hardware sequencers,
but with the critical feature that 90s samplers lack:
able to
resample, i.e. record while playing!
pop-up scratchpad for musical ideas.
low resource consumption, can stay open in background.
but flexible enough to allow expanding on compositions
human- and machine- readable project format
simple representation for project data
enable scripting and remapping.

data.title: Dr. Dobb's Journal interviews Jef Raskin (1986)
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Jef Raskin及其在用户界面（UI）设计方面的思想和作品的评价与讨论

不同观点：
• kstrauser认为过去的技术时代虽然有趣，但有很多不方便之处，不值得怀念。他通过回顾旧杂志中的广告（如Emacs、C编译器、vi移植等）来展示早期技术产品的价格高昂和局限性。
• uxhacker指出Jef Raskin在《The Humane Interface》一书中对人类思维与计算机交互之间差距的关注，尤其是在AI时代，Raskin的理念变得更加相关。他认为AI有可能实现真正人性化的界面，但也挑战了Raskin的一些假设。
• NoFunPedant分享了自己在大学时使用Canon Cat（由Raskin设计）的经历，尽管他是完全的新手，但仍觉得Cat难以理解，而Macintosh则容易上手。这个 anecdote 显示了Raskin的设计并不适合所有人。
• PaulDavisThe1st批评了Raskin的界面设计，认为其设计只是个人偏好的体现，而不是深具洞察力的创新。他质疑Raskin的设计是否真的具有普遍适用性。
• codepoet80猜测如果Raskin看到今天的iPhone或现代Mac，可能会感到失望，暗示现代设备背离了Raskin的初衷。
• omnibrain提到Dr. Dobb's网站的保存问题，指出尽管该网站承诺保留计算历史，但实际上链接多有损坏。
• kristianp分享了Raskin曾销售的Apple II产品Swyftcard的链接，为讨论提供了背景信息。
• OhMeadhbh表示自己仍然在日常使用Canon Cat，并对其表示喜爱，展示了Raskin设计仍有忠实用户。
• drivers99正在制作一个类似Canon Cat的键盘，并计划使用微控制器或65c02开发软件，显示了Raskin设计对后续技术爱好者的影响。

补充讨论：
• janfoeh幽默地评论了操作系统的本质，认为它总是给用户带来挑战。
• LaundroMat提到在阅读关于技术交互挫折的文章时，遭遇了cookie弹窗问题，讽刺了技术使用中的小烦恼。
• pixelpoet注意到Jef Raskin的儿子Aza Raskin长得非常像他，提供了一个与讨论相关的个人观察。
• Rochus引用了一句有趣的话来评论等待计算机响应的烦恼。
• keeganpoppen高度评价了Raskin的《The Humane Interface》，认为它是任何关心UI/UX的人必读之作，显示了对Raskin思想的强烈支持。

争议的焦点：Raskin的设计理念是否真正具有广泛适用性和深刻洞察力，还是仅为个人偏好的体现。PaulDavisThe1st和NoFunPedant的经历显示了对Raskin设计实用性的怀疑，而OhMeadhbh和keeganpoppen则表示了支持和喜爱。

• NoFunPedant分享了自己在大学时使用Canon Cat（由Raskin设计）的经历，尽管他是完全的新手，但仍觉得Cat难以理解，而Macintosh则容易上手。这个 anecdote 显示了Raskin的设计并不适合所有人。
• PaulDavisThe1st批评了Raskin的界面设计，认为其设计只是个人偏好的体现，而不是深具洞察力的创新。他质疑Raskin的设计是否真的具有普遍适用性。
• codepoet80猜测如果Raskin看到今天的iPhone或现代Mac，可能会感到失望，暗示现代设备背离了Raskin的初衷。

• kristianp分享了Raskin曾销售的Apple II产品Swyftcard的链接，为讨论提供了背景信息。
• OhMeadhbh表示自己仍然在日常使用Canon Cat，并对其表示喜爱，展示了Raskin设计仍有忠实用户。
• drivers99正在制作一个类似Canon Cat的键盘，并计划使用微控制器或65c02开发软件，显示了Raskin设计对后续技术爱好者的影响。

补充讨论：
• janfoeh幽默地评论了操作系统的本质，认为它总是给用户带来挑战。
• LaundroMat提到在阅读关于技术交互挫折的文章时，遭遇了cookie弹窗问题，讽刺了技术使用中的小烦恼。
• pixelpoet注意到Jef Raskin的儿子Aza Raskin长得非常像他，提供了一个与讨论相关的个人观察。
• Rochus引用了一句有趣的话来评论等待计算机响应的烦恼。
• keeganpoppen高度评价了Raskin的《The Humane Interface》，认为它是任何关心UI/UX的人必读之作，显示了对Raskin思想的强烈支持。

争议的焦点：Raskin的设计理念是否真正具有广泛适用性和深刻洞察力，还是仅为个人偏好的体现。PaulDavisThe1st和NoFunPedant的经历显示了对Raskin设计实用性的怀疑，而OhMeadhbh和keeganpoppen则表示了支持和喜爱。

data.title: Improving Naval Ship Acquisition
data.author: Luc
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了美国海军舰船建造中存在的延误和超支问题，并提出了改进建议。文章指出，当前海军舰船设计复杂、功能多重，导致成本和建造时间大幅增加。例如，福特级航母配备的高端雷达增加了设计复杂性和成本，而 littoral combat ship (LCS) 因尝试承担多种角色而提前退役。文章建议：1) 设计更简单、用途单一的舰船；2) 将设计工作从第三方收回，由海军内部完成，并增加海军建筑师人数；3) 在设计基本完成前，不应开始建造。这些措施旨在减少成本超支和工期延误，提高海军舰船建造效率。

This is a policy proposal written by
Austin Vernon
and myself for improving US naval shipbuilding. It was produced for
Rebuilding.tech
, a techno-industrial policy playbook curated by
IFP
,
FAI
, and
American Compass
.
USS Iowa, one of the many WWII-era ships designed in-house by the Navy.
US Naval vessels today regularly take far longer to build than scheduled, and greatly exceed their already-high cost estimates. A
2018 GAO report
found that more than 80% of both lead ships (the first ship built of a series) and follow-on ships (subsequent ships of the series) were over budget, sometimes dramatically so. The first
Zumwalt-class destroyer
was over budget by 38%, and the first two
Littoral Combat Ships
were over budget by 150%.
Similarly, of eight lead ships reviewed by the GAO, every one was delivered behind schedule, and five of the eight ships were delivered two years late or more. Delays and cost overruns are wasteful and hamper the effectiveness of the Navy: reducing them would mean getting more ships, faster.
Delays and cost overruns are in part driven by the Navy’s ship design and acquisition process. Broadly speaking, the Navy creates high-level requirements for complex, multi-role ships, and then outsources the design of these ships to third-party contractors. Once a design is selected, it is turned into production drawings (so-called “detail designs”), which are used to produce the ships. In an effort to reduce the time it takes to deliver a ship, ship construction is often started before ship design is complete. However, this strategy frequently backfires: as design work is completed, changes to under-construction ships are often required, resulting in costly and time-consuming rework.
We recommend several changes to this process to reduce cost and schedule growth, and to reliably deliver ships faster and for less cost.
Instead of complex, multi-role ships which have expensive and often unnecessary features, the Navy should focus on simpler ships with narrower use cases.
Rather than outsourcing design to third parties, ship design should be brought in-house, and NAVSEA should expand its staff of Naval Architects from around 300 to closer to 1200.
Production on ships should not begin until design is substantially completed.
Simple ships
Many of the US Navy’s recent ship designs are large, complex multi-role ships. The Navy expects the same ship to hunt pirates, counter ballistic missiles, track submarines, and more. Also common are high-end features unnecessary for a ship’s mission. These complex ships have many negative consequences on the ability to design ships, increase production throughput, and meet budget and schedule targets. A return to simpler ships would help the Navy deliver more ships on time and within budget.
A few examples of scope bloat:
Ford-class carriers
have high-end radars with similar capabilities as the radars of guided-missile destroyers. Yet they do not have long range surface-to-air missiles, they are surrounded by escorts with similar capabilities, and the emissions from these radars make them easier to detect, track, and target. The cost of the systems is substantial (likely more than $1 billion after including support systems), and they add design complexity and construction time.
Recent
Burke-class destroyers
have extensive helicopter facilities, despite their main role being vehicles for offensive and defensive missiles. The helicopters add significant cost, weight, and crew to the ship. The Flight III ships, first launched in 2023, also have a much larger radar jammed into the same hull.
The
Littoral Combat Ship
(LCS) was supposed to be a jack of all trades, filling roles like patrol or minesweeping by swapping out modules. But LCS ships are undergoing rapid early retirement because the attempt to fill so many roles compromised many attributes, and designing modules proved unworkable. Even worse, many specialist ship roles, like minesweeping, are now being retired without replacements because the LCS failed to fill the role.
Frigates are typically smaller and less heavily armed than more capable and more expensive destroyers. But the new
Constellation-class frigate
will cost nearly as much as the Burke-class destroyer, because of its extensive radar and missile capacity. The bloated design missed an opportunity to complement the Burke by being strong where the Burke is weaker, like anti-submarine warfare.
The extra features raise cost, hurt producibility, and can even compromise ship effectiveness.
A likely cause for this scope bloat is the adherence to the “
Distributed Maritime Operations
” doctrine, or DMO. The logic is that a traditional battlegroup is too vulnerab

data.title: Stop using REST for state synchronization (2024)
data.author: Kerrick
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了使用REST接口在客户端和服务器之间同步状态的弊端，并建议采用更合适的状态同步协议。作者指出，REST是一种状态传输协议，而大多数应用实际上需要的是状态同步。这种不匹配导致开发者必须在REST之上实现临时的状态同步逻辑，增加了复杂性和脆弱性。

作者通过一个简单的文本输入框例子展示了使用REST时所需的繁琐代码，包括处理初始值获取、显示加载状态和错误信息等。这种模式不仅产生大量样板代码，而且在处理并发请求时可能出现错误，比如当用户快速连续更改值时，请求顺序可能无法保证。

因此，作者建议用专门的状态同步协议取代REST，以简化开发并提高可靠性。这将使开发者只需关注界面显示和数据位置，而不必处理繁杂的状态传输逻辑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：REST是否适用于实时状态同步，以及可能的替代方案

不同观点：
• kokanee认为REST在处理实时同步UI时表现不足，尤其是当多个用户同时与UI元素交互时，挑战更大。他指出，虽然冲突解决可以通过现有方案抽象处理，但UI行为的具体细节处理仍然复杂。他认为当前的本地状态维护和集中存储的平衡是合理的，但很多应用在维护本地状态方面做得不够好。

• gregw2提出了两种解决方案来处理REST和同步状态的问题：一是获取数据时同时获取版本号，以确保数据更新时的匹配；二是发送信息时同时包含新旧值，以防止数据冲突。

• qudat同意状态同步是前端开发的一个热门话题，并指出很多API将复杂性推给了前端。虽然GraphQL是一个选项，但调整它并不简单，而CRDTs在大多数组织中并不常见。因此，完全抛弃REST并不现实。

• jemmyw认为虽然CRDT或OT是可选方案，但其实施复杂，尤其是在改造现有系统时。应根据具体的使用场景决定是否需要复杂的 state sync。

• cgio主张REST并不适用于状态同步，CRDTs也只是在最终一致性上有一定作用。他指出分布式数据存储或数据库复制等才是“已解决”的状态同步问题。

• kobieps对同步引擎持乐观态度，认为文中所描述的痛点确实存在。

• coolhand2120质疑将HTTP称为REST的合理性，并指出CRUD API与REST的区别。他认为如果不采用事件溯源或CRDT等协议，很多状态同步问题难以解决。

• sansseriff提到从REST过渡到CRDTs的资源和教程不足，导致这种转变在实际应用中并不常见。

• 4b11b4提到Electric SQL看起来不错，但未实际使用过。

• toomim介绍了Braid项目，认为HTTP需要从状态转移协议进化到状态同步协议。Braid扩展已经实现了这一目标，并详细解释了其工作原理和优势。

• AtlasBarfed提到CAP定理在这一讨论中的重要性，指出在客户端可靠性高度可变的情况下，需要考虑CP或AP的选择。

• yakshaving_jgt认为文章虽然指出了REST在状态同步上的不足，但并未提供明确的替代方案。

• 3cats-in-a-coat认为通过保持资源不可变和传递根资源，REST上的状态同步可以变得相对简单。

• gxs认为完全抛弃REST并不恰当，指出在某些场景下REST是完全可以接受的，但在批量同步大数据时可能不合适。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于REST是否适用于状态同步，以及在何种场景下应选择其他方案如CRDTs或GraphQL。
• 讨论中也涉及了具体技术实现的复杂性，以及现有方案在实际应用中的可行性和资源可用性问题。
• 另外，Braid项目的介绍为状态同步问题提供了一种可能的解决方案，并引发了对HTTP协议未来发展的讨论。

tl;dr
: Most apps need state
synchronization
, not state
transfer
. We should replace
REST and friends with proper state synchronization protocols where
appropriate.
Apart from getting into van life in Europe and working on the
Eqlog
Datalog engine,
I’ve also spent some time of my sabbatical building various webapps. The
tech stack I used was React + Typescript for the frontend and a REST
server implemented with Rust and the Axum library as backend. Rust might
be somewhat unusual, but I think otherwise this is a very typical
setup.
What struck me is how incredibly cumbersome, repetitive and brittle
this programming model is, and I think much of this is due to using REST
as interface between the client and the server. REST is a state
transfer
protocol, but we usually want to
synchronize
a piece of state between the client and the server. This mismatch means
that we usually implement ad-hoc state synchronization on top of REST,
and it turns out that this is not entirely trivial and actually
incredibly cumbersome to get right.
It’s probably easiest to explain what I mean with an example that’s
part of most webapps in some variant: An input element that allows the
user to edit a piece of text that is saved to the backend database.
Using REST we can model this as a path, say
/api/foo
, that
supports GET and POST methods to fetch or replace the text by a given
value (perhaps also DELETE and PUT if you want to complicate things). A
React component that allows users to edit this piece of text will
probably display a text input element, GET the initial value when the
component is created and POST a new value when the text input loses

43997286.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了使用REST接口在客户端和服务器之间同步状态的弊端，并建议采用更合适的状态同步协议。作者指出，REST是一种状态传输协议，而大多数应用实际上需要的是状态同步。这种不匹配导致开发者必须在REST之上实现临时的状态同步逻辑，增加了复杂性和脆弱性。

作者通过一个简单的文本输入框例子展示了使用REST时所需的繁琐代码，包括处理初始值获取、显示加载状态和错误信息等。这种模式不仅产生大量样板代码，而且在处理并发请求时可能出现错误，比如当用户快速连续更改值时，请求顺序可能无法保证。

因此，作者建议用专门的状态同步协议取代REST，以简化开发并提高可靠性。这将使开发者只需关注界面显示和数据位置，而不必处理繁杂的状态传输逻辑。
43997286.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：REST是否适用于实时状态同步，以及可能的替代方案

不同观点：
• kokanee认为REST在处理实时同步UI时表现不足，尤其是当多个用户同时与UI元素交互时，挑战更大。他指出，虽然冲突解决可以通过现有方案抽象处理，但UI行为的具体细节处理仍然复杂。他认为当前的本地状态维护和集中存储的平衡是合理的，但很多应用在维护本地状态方面做得不够好。

• gregw2提出了两种解决方案来处理REST和同步状态的问题：一是获取数据时同时获取版本号，以确保数据更新时的匹配；二是发送信息时同时包含新旧值，以防止数据冲突。

• qudat同意状态同步是前端开发的一个热门话题，并指出很多API将复杂性推给了前端。虽然GraphQL是一个选项，但调整它并不简单，而CRDTs在大多数组织中并不常见。因此，完全抛弃REST并不现实。

• jemmyw认为虽然CRDT或OT是可选方案，但其实施复杂，尤其是在改造现有系统时。应根据具体的使用场景决定是否需要复杂的 state sync。

• cgio主张REST并不适用于状态同步，CRDTs也只是在最终一致性上有一定作用。他指出分布式数据存储或数据库复制等才是“已解决”的状态同步问题。

• kobieps对同步引擎持乐观态度，认为文中所描述的痛点确实存在。

• coolhand2120质疑将HTTP称为REST的合理性，并指出CRUD API与REST的区别。他认为如果不采用事件溯源或CRDT等协议，很多状态同步问题难以解决。

• sansseriff提到从REST过渡到CRDTs的资源和教程不足，导致这种转变在实际应用中并不常见。

• 4b11b4提到Electric SQL看起来不错，但未实际使用过。

• toomim介绍了Braid项目，认为HTTP需要从状态转移协议进化到状态同步协议。Braid扩展已经实现了这一目标，并详细解释了其工作原理和优势。

• AtlasBarfed提到CAP定理在这一讨论中的重要性，指出在客户端可靠性高度可变的情况下，需要考虑CP或AP的选择。

• yakshaving_jgt认为文章虽然指出了REST在状态同步上的不足，但并未提供明确的替代方案。

• 3cats-in-a-coat认为通过保持资源不可变和传递根资源，REST上的状态同步可以变得相对简单。

• gxs认为完全抛弃REST并不恰当，指出在某些场景下REST是完全可以接受的，但在批量同步大数据时可能不合适。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于REST是否适用于状态同步，以及在何种场景下应选择其他方案如CRDTs或GraphQL。
• 讨论中也涉及了具体技术实现的复杂性，以及现有方案在实际应用中的可行性和资源可用性问题。
• 另外，Braid项目的介绍为状态同步问题提供了一种可能的解决方案，并引发了对HTTP协议未来发展的讨论。

data.title: GTK Krell Monitors
data.author: Deeg9rie9usi
data.article_summary: GKrellM是一款系统监控软件，支持主题定制，能够显示主机名、时钟、CPU（支持多核监控）、温度、风扇、电压等信息。它还具备进程监控、磁盘监控、网络监控（包括TCP连接和流量图表）、内存和交换空间使用情况、文件系统状态以及邮件箱监控等功能。每个传感器监控都有可配置的警告和警报。GKrellM可以通过单进程管理多个监控，减少系统负载，并支持插件扩展。它可以在Linux、FreeBSD、Mac OS X、NetBSD、OpenBSD和Windows上运行，且提供多种主题和包下载。用户可通过邮件列表、Matrix房间和IRC频道获取支持和交流。GKrellM是基于GNU GPL许可的自由软件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GKrellM及其相关开源项目的技术价值、现状及未来发展

不同观点：
• 一些用户对GKrellM及其 creator Bill Wilson表示怀念与感激。例如，jchoksi提到Bill开发的PiKrellCam是树莓派上最佳的音视频录制和运动检测程序，并对Bill的逝世表示惋惜。gsmethells也提到从1998年开始使用GKrellM，并对其终身开源贡献表示感谢。
• 技术更新与维护的必要性。Deeg9rie9usi指出GKrellM仍在使用被弃用的GTK2，并呼吁开发者贡献代码以维护项目。这一观点强调了开源项目需要社区的持续贡献。
• GKrellM在现代系统上的适用性问题。merpkz认为在平铺窗口管理器（如i3wm和awesome wm）环境下，GKrellM不再实用，因为窗口总是全屏显示，使其失去原有的功能。nubinetwork也提到在多核和多硬盘系统上，GKrellM的显示能力不足。
• 用户对GKrellM的怀旧与重新发现。例如，ninkendo和sigmonsays提到在多年前使用过GKrellM，并在今天重新认识到其价值。ninkendo还分享了一个具体的工作场景，说明GKrellM在监控内存使用上的实用性。
• 技术实现与用户体验的讨论。zxcvgm分享了自己通过阅读源码并贡献补丁的经历，强调了开源软件的价值。kijiki和sph提到GKrellM的客户端/服务器模式及在老旧硬件上的高效运行。

补充讨论：
• 对于GKrellM名称的来源，cadamsdotcom提到可能是参考了1956年电影《禁忌星球》中的“Id Monster”概念，并请求事实核查。
• 用户对现代监控工具的看法。sph认为现代监控工具（如Electron或Python编写）可能过于笨重，不如C语言编写的老工具高效。

争议焦点：
• GKrellM在现代计算环境中的适用性及其技术更新问题。一些用户认为其在多核、多硬盘及平铺窗口管理器环境下不再适用，强调了技术更新的必要性。

43970057.article_content:
Themes_Doc
Plugins
GKrellM is a single process stack of system monitors which supports
applying themes to match its appearance to your window
manager, Gtk, or any other theme.
1
2
Builtin Features
Hostname/systemname display.
Clock/calendar.
SMP CPU monitor that can chart individual CPUs and/or a composite CPU.
Temperature, fan, and voltage sensor monitors if supported by the
kernel and the mainboard hardware.
Linux requires lm_sensors modules, sysfs sensors for kernels >= 2.6.0
or a running mbmon daemon. Sensors can also be read from mbmon on
FreeBSD. On Linux, you can also monitor disk temperatures from the
hddtemp daemon and nvidia GPU temperatures if nvidia-settings is
installed.
Each sensor monitor has a configurable alarm and warning.
Process monitor with a chart for load and forks and a display of number
of current processes and users.
Disk monitor that can chart individual disks or a composite disk.
Internet monitor (http, ftp, ...) that displays current tcp port
connections and charts historical port hits for over two days.
Net interface monitors with charts for all routed net interfaces.
Data rx/tx LEDs and a timer button that can
be linked to a ppp or isdn net interface and displays on line time.
Memory and swap space usage meters, and a swap page in/out chart.
File system meters which show capacity/free space and can mount/umount.
A mailbox monitor which can launch a mail reader, a mail fetch/check
program, and a sound notify command. Builtin new mail message checking
for mbox, maildir, MH, POP3, and IMAP mailboxes.
APM laptop battery meter with a configurable alarm and warning for
low battery time left.
Uptime display.
Multiple monitors managed by a single process to reduce system load.
Charts have auto scaling or fixed scaling modes.
Commands can be configured to run when monitor labels are clicked.
gkrellm can run in client mode and collect data from a gkrellmd
server running on a remote machine.
Both gkrellm and the gkrellmd server are plugin capable so special
interest monitors can be coded.
Screenshots
1: The CPU chart's nice time (green) is de-emphasized
by splitting it into a small view, and the sys time is inverted.
The disk hda chart is split at the 50% point.
The 5 volt supply is triggering a warning. The animated penguin is
announcing there is new mail.
Three audio plugins are shown enabled:
GKrellMSS sound scope, Volume, and GKrellMMS . See the plugins
page for these and many more interesting plugins.
2: A more simple configuration with nice time hidden and
two net interfaces being monitored. The battery time left
is triggering an alarm. The theme is one I put together as a test
and demo for the new frame overlap features for 2.1.x. So if you
run 2.1.x and like it or want hints on using the new features
in making your own theme, here's the
hardware theme
.
And if you're wondering why I call it
"hardware", it's because it has an alternative that looks like
this
.
System Requirements
GKrellM requires
Gtk+ 2.24
or newer.
The GKrellM server (gkrellmd) requires only
GLib 2.32
or newer and
may be installed on servers that do not have Gtk+ or X11. See the INSTALL
file.
Linux:
data is read from the /proc filesystem.
FreeBSD:
a version may be compiled using code contributed by
Hajimu UMEMOTO
Mac OS X:
a version may be compiled using code contributed by
Ben Hines
NetBSD / OpenBSD:
a version may be compiled using code contributed
by
Anthony Mallet
Windows:
A GKrellM that runs on Windows is provided by
Stefan Gehn
at
his site
.
Package Downloads
GKrellM is available in many Linux and BSD distributions as well as for macOS and Windows.
Arch Linux package
Debian
Package

Homebrew formula for macOS and Linux

OpenSUSE Package

Source Code
The GKrellM source code repository is at
https://git.srcbox.net/gkrellm/gkrellm
The latest source code release is
gkrellm-2.4.0.tar.bz2
.
Previous source code releases can be found in the
releases directory
.
Contact
There are several ways to get in touch with GKrellM users and developers:
For
usage questions
there is a
mailing list
that you can subscribe to.
To
chat
about GKrellM with other users there is a Matrix room
#gkrellm:srcbox.net
.
In addition there is an IRC channel
#gkrellm on irc.libera.chat
,
which you can
access through your browser
or with any IRC client.
If you discover either a
bug
or have a
feature
suggestion for GKrellm, feel free to
open an issue
.
Links
Here are some instructional or interesting links about GKrellM:

Themes on gnome-look.org
Mike Edwards wrote a
PHP library
useful for PHP developers who want to get information out of a gkrellmd server.
William Stearns'
gkrellmd over SSH tutorial
.
Christopher Carey shows how you can even
monitor a TiVo with gkrellmd
.
Bryson Borg has done a similar gkrellmd port for a
firmware modified Linksys WRT54G router
.
GKrellM is
free
software released under the GNU General Public

data.title: Ollama's new engine for multimodal models
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: Ollama推出了新的多模态模型引擎，支持如Meta Llama 4、Google Gemma 3、Qwen 2.5 VL和Mistral Small 3.1等模型。引擎具备多模态理解和推理能力，例如通过Llama 4 Scout分析图片内容并回答相关问题，支持多张图片输入及关系分析（如Gemma 3），以及文档扫描和字符识别（如Qwen 2.5 VL）。Ollama的新引擎旨在提高本地推理的可靠性和准确性，并为未来支持更多模态（如语音、图像生成、视频生成等）奠定基础。该引擎还注重模型模块化和社区贡献，以增强功能和工具支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ollama新引擎的发布及其技术实现，以及与llama.cpp的关系和多模态支持

不同观点：
• simonw认为Ollama选择此时发布新引擎可能与其早已在开发多模态功能有关，且独立于llama.cpp有利于掌控自己的发展方向。
• andy_xor_andrew希望看到更多关于新引擎实现的细节，特别是如何通过Go调用GGML库，并指出这些细节应在博客中更明显地展示。
• oezi指出多模态应包括文本、图像、音频甚至视频，而不仅仅是图像生成或分析，并强调了区分不同多模态模型的重要性。
• clpm4j对LLM领域中多种相似命名（如llama相关的各种项目）感到困惑，认为这可能会导致混淆。

争议焦点：
• yossi_peti和ac29分别指出了Ollama示例中的中文翻译错误和交通建议错误，质疑示例的准确性和专业性。

补充讨论：
• tommica提问为什么有些人对Ollama持有负面看法，通常得到的建议是自行运行llama.cpp。
• bradly关注Ollama的Docker集成在支持图像和视频处理时如何应对GPU使用问题。
• mark_l_watson询问社区中有哪些有趣且实用的多模态项目，以寻求个人项目灵感。
• JKCalhoun关心Ollama是否支持类似ChatGPT的用户上下文功能，特别是初始提示和保存的上下文历史。
• Koshima从更广泛的LLM趋势角度分析，认为Ollama新引擎的发布顺应了多模态体验的整合趋势，可能对开发实时、上下文丰富的应用具有变革意义。
• newusertoday质疑Ollama为何每次新模型出现时都需要升级以提供支持。

这些讨论揭示了社区对Ollama新引擎的技术细节、示例准确性、Docker集成、用户功能以及多模态支持的广泛关注和不同看法。

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何在Rust中构建一个无锁的固定大小数组`LockFreeArray<T, N>`，该数组使用原子操作和自由列表在多线程环境下存储和交换堆分配的值，而无需锁。文章详细讲解了如何使用`AtomicPtr`、`AtomicUsize`和`compare_exchange`等工具，以及内存顺序的重要性。无锁编程虽然速度快，但非常复杂且容易出错，需要开发者手动保证线程安全。文章还提供了具体代码实现，包括数组的初始化、尝试插入值和取出值的方法，并通过标记索引解决了ABA问题。总的来说，无锁编程类似于高风险的活动，虽然高效但需要极高的谨慎和技巧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于无锁数据结构的性能、实现细节、适用场景及相关技术讨论

不同观点：
• gpderetta认为，无锁数组并不一定比有锁变体更快。无锁数组每次操作都需要执行一次CAS（Compare-And-Swap），这可能会成为性能瓶颈。相比之下，普通的互斥锁只需要两次CAS操作。如果互斥锁变体使用自由列表，性能差异也可以被解释。他强调无锁并不自动意味着更快，且基准测试需要谨慎对待。

• Animats分享了在Rust中进行无锁编程的实际案例，涉及在GPU和CPU之间同步状态。他指出无锁编程在特定场景下非常有用，例如无法直接读取某些状态时。

• MobiusHorizons对文中过度强调无锁数据结构的“危险性”和违规性表示不满，认为这种描述显得幼稚，并指出任何高度优化的结构都有其权衡和适用范围。

• tombert表示对Rust中的无锁结构感兴趣，但平常避免使用锁，而更倾向于使用Tokio channels进行并发处理，因为觉得锁难以推理。

Lock-Free Rust: How to Build a Rollercoaster While Itâs on Fire
.
Posted on
2025-05-12
Author: Julian Goldstein
âEvery stitch in that flag was a commitment to thread safety without locks.
std::atomic
was the needle.â
â Betsy Ross, Federalist Papers, Draft 29 (suppressed), 1782
Buckle your seatbelts, grab a helmet, and say goodbye to your loved ones because over the next few minutes, I am going to teach you more about lock-free data structures in RustÂ than any human being should reasonably know without a psychiatric evaluation.
So sit down, shut up, and pretend you understand memory ordering, because thread safety is just a social construct and
Ordering::Relaxed
is just denial with extra steps.
TL;DR
Weâre buildingÂ
LockFreeArray<T, N>
, a fixed-size, lock-free array for storing heap-allocated values. It uses atomics and a freelist to insert and take values across threadsÂ
without locks
. Youâll learn:
HowÂ
AtomicPtr
,Â
AtomicUsize
, andÂ
compare_exchange
Â work.
Why memory ordering matters (and how to screw it up).
Where this kind of thing is useful (task slots, freelists, fixed-resource pools).
And why it's generally a terrible idea unless you're very desperate or very clever.
If you enjoy the read and want to see more content like this please check out our product
yeet
or our
sandbox
. Thank you.
Lock-Free: The Decathlon of Danger
Lock-free programming exists for the same reason people free solo climb cliffs without ropes: itâs fast, itâs elegant, and it absolutely will kill you if you do it wrong. Here at
yeet
, we have become masters in this. Specifically when it comes to building high-performance priority queues for real-time streaming of high volume events from BPF ring buffers.
WithÂ
Mutex<T>
Â andÂ
RwLock<T>
, you get warm, fuzzy guarantees â mutual exclusion, fairness, and the comfort of compile-time safety at the expense of speed. On the other hand, with lock-free, you get speed â but it's entirely on you to keep it safe. No waiting, no blocking, no help.
Itâs the difference between riding a rollercoaster and building one mid-air while itâs on fire â and youâre also the passenger.
Congratulations â if youâre still reading, youâve officially decided to ignore your therapist, ghost the borrow checker, and raw-dog concurrency.
Meet The Atomics
You donât need all of them â just the dangerous few:
AtomicPtr<T>
Think raw pointers, but in a shared haunted house. You can pass ownership between threads, but if you screw up, the ghost of undefined behavior will visit you at runtime.
AtomicUsize
Used for indexing and freelist linkage. Itâs a plain old number, except itâs watched 24 / 7 by the CPUâs race condition alarm.
Ordering::{Acquire, Release, AcqRel, Relaxed}
These decide
when
other threads can see your changes. Use the wrong one and your writes arrive out of order, like sending a cake before the ovenâs even preheated.
Thatâs it. Three tools. Infinite ways to wake up in a hospital wrapped in unsafe.
Lock-Free Arrays: Index at Your Own Risk
This isnât your friendly neighborhood
Vec<T>
. This is
Vec<Violence>
.
No resizing. No bounds checks. No cozy locks to hold your hand when the threads start racing. Just raw pointers, atomics, and the kind of confidence that comes from skimming half the docs, pounding gas station coffee, and whispering
âhow hard could it be?â
Weâll call it
LockFreeArray<T, N>
Think of it as a fixed-size concurrent slot buffer â useful for task pools, on-demand workers, or resource slots that canât afford a lock.
It has three methods:
new()
Initializes the array and sets up a freelist of available slots.
try_insert(value: T) -> Result<usize, T>
Tries to place a value in an empty slot. On success, returns the index. On failure, returns your value back, gently but firmly.
take(index: usize) -> Option<T>
Removes and returns the value
T
at the given
index
. If itâs already empty, returns
None
.

data.title: Náhuatl and Mayan Language Renaissance Occurring in Mexico
data.author: bryanrasmussen
data.article_summary: 墨西哥拥有68种官方认可的土著语言，近700万人使用，包括玛雅语和纳瓦特尔语。然而，由于城市化、全球化以及西班牙语和英语的主导地位，许多土著语言正面临消亡的威胁。为保护这一丰富的语言遗产，墨西哥政府启动了土著语言课程和双语课程的计划。在尤卡坦州，约35,000名学生可以选择学习尤卡坦玛雅语。墨西哥城将有78所学校开设纳瓦特尔语课程。尽管资源有限和方言差异等挑战依然存在，学生和社区的热情日益增长，显示出土著语言在墨西哥身份认同中的持久价值。同时，土著语言还面临着历史遗留的歧视问题，保护这些语言不仅是保存词汇，更是维护土著人民的尊严和身份。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• [jf的观点] 认为纳瓦特尔语在墨西哥的复兴可能与墨西哥的“印第根主义运动”有关，并对纳瓦特尔语在墨西哥西班牙语及全球语言中的影响感到着迷。个人家族历史也激发了其对这一语言的兴趣。
• [dhosek的观点] 指出“玛雅语言”这一术语具有误导性，因为玛雅文化包含多种语言，而不仅仅是单一的语言。同时强调了墨西哥是世界上语言最多样化的国家之一，但人们往往将原住民文化扁平化，误认为某些文化已经灭绝。
• [eschulz的观点] 分享了个人经历，指出在墨西哥仍有许多年轻人讲土著语言（如萨波特克语），强调了土著语言在现代墨西哥社会中的实际存在。
• [ogogmad的观点] 提出是否有可能复兴玛雅象形文字，即便是在有限的形式下。
• [neilshev的观点] 对濒危语言的复兴持悲观态度，指出尽管有努力恢复（如爱尔兰的盖尔语），但成效不佳。认为在全球化背景下，本土语言容易被视为“无用”或“古老”，复兴非常困难，除非采取强制措施。
• [stackedinserter的观点] 持现实主义态度，认为在全球主流语言（如英语、西班牙语）的强大吸引力下，土著语言很难复兴。除非社会结构发生变化（如回到村落生活），否则趋势难以逆转。
• [thunder-blue-3的观点] 认为墨西哥有更紧迫的问题（如暴力和基本人权问题）需要关注，不应优先考虑语言复兴问题。

43974461.article_content:
Mexico is home to 68 officially recognized Indigenous languages, spoken by nearly 7 million people, including Mayan and Náhuatl. Yet, despite their historical significance, many of these languages are in decline. Urbanization, globalization, and the dominance of Spanish and English are slowly but surely pushing them to the brink.
To preserve Mexico’s rich linguistic heritage, Mexican authorities have kick-started an initiative to offer Indigenous language classes, and, in some cases, fully bilingual curriculums.
In Yucatán, efforts to teach the Maya language in schools are gaining momentum as 35,000 students from 75 municipalities now
have the option to study Yucatec-Maya
, beginning as early as grade school.
Náhuatl and Mayan Language Renaissance
The broader initiative includes efforts to preserve and revitalize Indigenous culture by recognizing the importance of Mexico’s Prehispanic heritage and how it connects with its cultural and historical significance.
The Mexican government’s commitment to this cause is reflected in the General Law of Linguistic Rights of Indigenous Peoples, which recognizes Indigenous languages as having equal validity with Spanish.
In Mexico City,
78 schools
will begin offering Náhuatl language classes in the next few weeks. Although Náhuatl is the most widely spoken Indigenous language on the entire American continent, it shows signs of quickly vanishing, especially among younger generations.
Classical age Maya stelae of Yaxilan depict two nobles in conversation. Photo: Carlos Rosado van der Gracht / Yucatán Magazine
“Náhuatl has since time immemorial been the language of the people of the valley of Mexico, but it’s not just a tongue of the past. It must be preserved as a living language into the future as part of our nation’s heritage,” said Mexico City Mayor Clara Brugada.
Across the country, similar initiatives are underway to promote the use of Indigenous languages like Zapotec and Mixtec, which have been spoken for centuries but now face the threat of extinction.
These classes are designed to teach vocabulary and grammar and immerse students in the cultural context of the languages. Through storytelling, traditional songs, and rituals, students gain a deeper understanding of the worldviews embedded in these ancient tongues.
In Yucatán, adult students can enroll in
Mayan language
classes at
INDEMAYA
, the Autonomous University of Yucatán, the Municipal Mayan Language Academy “Itzamná,” as well as at the UNAM’s
Cephcis language center
.
Growing Enthusiasm  for Indigenous languages
While challenges such as limited resources and varying dialects persist, the growing enthusiasm among students and communities signals a promising future for Indigenous languages, ensuring they remain an enduring part of Mexico’s identity.
It is important to keep in mind that indigenous languages in Mexico, are often met with discrimination. This prejudice stems from a complex web of historical, social, and economic factors that continue to marginalize indigenous communities.
The roots of this discrimination trace back to the Spanish colonization of Mexico. Spanish colonizers imposed their language and culture, creating a hierarchy where indigenous languages were deemed inferior. This legacy of cultural erasure persists today, as Spanish remains the dominant language in education, media, and government, while indigenous languages are often excluded from these spaces.
Social and racial prejudices further compound the issue. Indigenous people, who are frequently among the poorest in Mexico, face stereotypes that label their languages and cultures as “backward” or “outdated.” Speaking an indigenous language can lead to discrimination in urban areas, where Spanish is seen as the language of opportunity and modernity.
The fight for indigenous languages in Mexico is not just about preserving words; it’s about reclaiming identity, dignity, and a place in a society that has long marginalized its native peoples. By embracing linguistic diversity, Mexico can move closer to a future where all its voices are heard and valued.
Carlos Rosado van der Gracht
Senior Editor Carlos Rosado van der Gracht is a Mexican expedition/Canadian photographer, adventure leader, and PhD candidate. Born in Mérida, Carlos holds multimedia, philosophy, and translation degrees from universities in Mexico, Canada and Norway.

43974461.article_summary: 墨西哥拥有68种官方认可的土著语言，近700万人使用，包括玛雅语和纳瓦特尔语。然而，由于城市化、全球化以及西班牙语和英语的主导地位，许多土著语言正面临消亡的威胁。为保护这一丰富的语言遗产，墨西哥政府启动了土著语言课程和双语课程的计划。在尤卡坦州，约35,000名学生可以选择学习尤卡坦玛雅语。墨西哥城将有78所学校开设纳瓦特尔语课程。尽管资源有限和方言差异等挑战依然存在，学生和社区的热情日益增长，显示出土著语言在墨西哥身份认同中的持久价值。同时，土著语言还面临着历史遗留的歧视问题，保护这些语言不仅是保存词汇，更是维护土著人民的尊严和身份。

data.title: Comma 3X: Initial Impressions
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Comma 3X设备的功能、合法性、安全性及其在驾驶中的应用，特别是对于有健康问题（如眩晕症）的驾驶者的适用性。

不同观点：
• Vasco和Havoc认为，让有严重眩晕症的人驾驶车辆是危险的，尤其是在紧急情况下无法保证控制车辆，这可能危及他人安全。Vasco提到不同地区对驾驶健康条件的法规不同，而Havoc则认为这种做法简直疯狂。
• Mscbuck对Comma 3X持积极态度，认为其在交通和高速驾驶中表现良好，尤其是在与原车系统对比时，驾驶体验更好，但他也提到新模型在训练架构上的改进不如预期。
• Shellfishgene对在美国可以安装此类开源硬件和软件以控制车辆转向和刹车表示惊讶，因为在其他地方，安装未经认证的汽车部件可能不合法。
• Edude03对开源项目的收费问题提出质疑，认为开放源代码并不等同于免费，且开发需要成本，因此对每月收费感到不满的人表示不理解。
• Theparanoid分享了个人使用Comma 3X的经验，认为其在高速公路驾驶中表现良好，但不适合城市街道。
• Nancyminusone对Comma Prime的广告过多表示不满，并对产品公开声称的某些功能表示怀疑，特别是关于眩晕症驾驶者的使用。
• Mtlynch表示对AI驾驶控制持怀疑态度，但希望有系统能提供驾驶安全反馈，帮助避免危险情况。
• Optimusprinceps和Krosaen则对Comma 3X的具体功能和法律责任问题表示困惑和担忧，尤其是产品使用中的责任归属和潜在风险。
• Farmdve对Comma设备的概念感兴趣，但对其安装和修改车辆固件的要求感到不安，尤其是涉及安全系统如ABS时。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Comma 3X设备的合法性、安全性及其对驾驶者（特别是健康状况特殊的驾驶者）的适用性。
• 不同用户对开源项目的收费和责任归属问题存在分歧。
• 实际使用经验分享显示出对产品功能和可靠性的不同看法，尤其是在高速和城市驾驶中的表现。
• 对AI驾驶辅助技术的信任问题和潜在法律责任是用户关注的重点。

data.title: Show HN: A free AI risk assessment tool for LLM applications
data.author: percyding99
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了如何使用GitHub账户登录TavoAI平台以访问AIRiskOps评估工具。用户需要同意服务条款和隐私政策才能继续登录。整个过程强调了使用已有GitHub账户进行登录的便捷性以及对相关条款的接受要求。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：该工具是否具备企业级安全性和合规性，是否适合在企业和严肃场合中使用。

不同观点：
• [hiatus的观点] 认为该工具需要通过如SOC 2或ISO 27001这样的审计，才能吸引大型企业用户。他指出，企业通常会期待有审计报告、渗透测试结果等安全保障，并在参与任何对话之前要求查看这些信息。

• [Cynddl的观点] 对该工具的GDPR合规性表示怀疑，指出其宣传中混用了GDPR和PII（美国概念），这在合规性上存在问题。Cynddl强调，GDPR使用的是“个人数据”的概念，而不是PII，这不仅仅是用词差异，还涉及到隐私保护的有效性问题。

• [alickz的观点] 对工具的创意表示赞赏，但指出网站上的“隐私”链接无法使用。同时，alickz关心该工具是否会使用扫描的代码库进行训练或其他用途。

• [Urahandystar的观点] 认为该工具可能更适合针对个人开发者或编程爱好者，而非企业市场。他建议通过小额交易来吸引个人用户，而非专注于企业市场。

补充讨论：
• 关于工具合规性的争议焦点在于其是否真正符合GDPR的要求，Cynddl指出其在合规性宣传上的不准确可能导致对隐私保护的误解。
• 安全性和透明度是hiatus关注的重点，他期望看到更多关于安全措施和审计结果的公开信息。
• alickz提出了对隐私保护实际操作的关切，尤其是对代码库的使用方式存在疑问。
• Urahandystar提出了市场定位的不同策略，认为个人开发者市场可能比企业市场更适合该工具。

这些观点共同构成了对该工具在安全性、合规性和市场定位上的多角度讨论。

data.title: Zinc Microcapacitors Are the Best of Both Worlds
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 研究人员开发了锌离子微型电容器，结合了电池和超级电容器的优点，适用于小型设备。这种锌微型电容器具备高能量密度和快速充放电的特点，有望在需要长寿命和小体积的电子设备中找到应用空间。相比传统电池，它更安全、环保，同时提供了更高的功率密度，填补了电池和超级电容器之间的技术空白。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同类型的能量存储技术及其在特定应用中的适用性，主要围绕传感器节点和能量采集应用展开。

不同观点：
• myself248认为锌基或其他高性能电池技术适合用于能量采集较慢、消耗间歇的传感器节点。这种情况下，不需要很大的能量容量，但需要良好的功率密度以支持突发传输，并且需要非常高的循环耐久性。

• westurner质疑为何选择锌，而非碳材料。他引用了关于碳纳米管纤维的研究，指出这些材料具有很高的能量存储能力（583 Wh/kg），尽管这是通过机械扭转实现的。他还提到石墨烯超级电容器通常比（微型）电容器具有较低的能量密度。

• dvh则对使用C0G型电容器提出疑问，暗示这种电容器可能已经具备足够的性能，无需转向其他材料或技术。

补充讨论：
• westurner引用的研究表明，碳基材料，尤其是纳米技术，可能在能量存储密度上具有显著优势。
• myself248的论点基于实际应用中的需求，如功率密度和循环耐久性，而不仅仅是能量密度。
• 争议的焦点在于不同材料和技术在特定应用中的实际优势，如锌 vs 碳材料，以及C0G电容器的适用性。
• 讨论中提到了多种技术选项，如超级电容器和机械能量存储方法，显示出对多种解决方案的开放态度。

Psychology and Behavior
You're Right! You Are Working Longer and Attending More Meetings
A study of 3 million people confirms what many work-from-home employees already know: We're swamped. Research by
Raffaella Sadun,
Jeffrey Polzer,
and colleagues.
Featuring
Raffaella Sadun
and
Jeffrey T. Polzer
.
By
Danielle Kost
on
September 14, 2020
.
Work-from-home employees whose days seem longer, with more meetings and emails than ever before, may find a new Harvard Business School study validating.
An analysis of the emails and meetings of 3.1 million people in 16 global cities found that the average workday increased by 8.2 percent—or 48.5 minutes—during the pandemic’s early weeks. Employees also participated in more meetings, though for less time than they did before COVID-19 sent many workers home.
“There is a general sense that we never stop being in front of Zoom or interacting,” says Raffaella Sadun, professor of business administration in the HBS Strategy Unit. “It’s very taxing, to be honest.”
Shifting to remote work at the start of the pandemic stripped away whatever was left of the elusive 9-to-5 business day and replaced it with videoconferencing and “asynchronous work.” With at least
16 percent of Americans
planning to keep working from home part of the time after COVID-19 abates, researchers are probing how virtual interaction might reshape organizations.
In the first large-scale analysis of digital communication early in the crisis, the team—Sadun; Jeffrey T. Polzer, the UPS Foundation Professor of Human Resource Management; HBS doctoral candidate Evan DeFilippis; New York University doctoral student Stephen Michael Impink; and former HBS research associate Madison Singell—studied aggregated, anonymous emails and meeting invitations of employees at 21,500 companies in North America, Europe, and the Middle East.
There is a general sense that we never stop being in front of Zoom or interacting. It’s very taxing, to be honest.
“The role of an office is to congregate and help people work together,” Sadun says. “For us, the question was, ‘What happens when you cannot have that physical space anymore?’ How do people adjust their work patterns?”
Longer days and more check-ins
The team compared the frequency and timing of emails sent within and outside organizations eight weeks before the start of pandemic-related lockdowns and eight weeks after. On average, they found that:
Employees sent 5.2 percent more emails a day.
Emails had 2.9 percent more recipients.
About 8.3 percent more emails were sent after business hours.
Sadun and Polzer also analyzed meeting invitations—the quantity, duration, and number of attendees—and observed that:
People attended 13 percent more meetings.
Each meeting was 12 minutes—or 20 percent—shorter, reducing the number of meeting hours by 12 percent, or 19 minutes.
The number of people invited to each meeting rose by two, or 14 percent.
Perhaps most striking: As researchers compared the time when people started sending emails and attending meetings each day and when they ended, they saw that the average workday lasted 8.2 percent longer, an extra 48.5 minutes. While it’s unlikely that employees worked continuously during that period, Sadun suspects that employees adopted more fluid schedules to accommodate interruptions from, say, a child struggling with virtual learning or a sick family member.
“Unless you really are able to create distinct boundaries between your life and your work, it's almost inevitable that we see these blurring lines,” she says.
The research team detailed their findings in the working paper
Collaborating During Coronavirus: The Impact of COVID-19 on the Nature of Work
, released by the National Bureau of Economic Research in July.
Probing the productivity and morale toll
The anonymized nature of the data made it difficult to discern the quality of the meetings and email communication, and the impact on employees’ well-being. The study also didn’t include the time spent on collaboration tools, such as Slack and Microsoft Teams, which have become increasingly popular.
To tackle some of these questions, Sadun has been studying how 300 knowledge workers have been spending their time during the pandemic and how those activities affect their moods and perceived effectiveness. So far, the preliminary conclusions have been highly varied and personal.
“This is one of those things where it’s hard to make one statement for everybody,” Sadun says. “If you have a large house, life is good. If you have to combine your bedroom with your office, it’s not as good.”
It doesn’t take a detailed time log to know that videoconferencing fatigue has long set in for many employees, a likely factor in shrinking meeting times. Gathering in person doesn’t seem as draining as staring at a screen.
“The issue with Zoom is that you’re always on there. You have to show a concentrated face the whole time,” she says. “It's very unnatural to be constantly looking attentive for hours.”

data.title: The first year of free-threaded Python
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary:
本文总结了Python社区在支持无全局解释器锁（GIL）的多线程版本方面所取得的进展。CPython 3.14.0b1的发布和PyCon 2025的召开标志着这一努力的重要里程碑。无GIL的Python能够更好地利用现代多核CPU和GPU的计算能力，但需要对许多依赖C扩展的包进行审核和修改以确保线程安全。

Quansight团队在多个方面做出了贡献，包括打包工具、绑定生成器、PyData生态系统的基础包及热门依赖包的支持。CPython核心开发者也进行了多项改进，如使warnings模块在无GIL构建中默认线程安全，修复asyncio和ctypes模块中的线程安全问题，以及提升垃圾回收器的性能。

一年前，Python包生态系统在无GIL构建中几乎完全无法运行，但现在情况已显著改善。本文还提到正在努力支持的其他流行包，并提供了一份详细指南以帮助其他开发者更新他们的包以支持无GIL的Python。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python中GIL（全局解释器锁）的移除及其潜在影响，以及多进程和多线程编程的优劣对比

不同观点：
• sgarland认为，多进程编程中进程间通信往往需要复制数据，成本较高，建议更多使用`SharedMemory`和`ShareableList`等工具来优化性能。
• pansa2关注GIL移除对多线程代码的影响，指出GIL的存在不仅是因为多线程代码依赖它，还因为去除GIL会使解释器实现和C扩展变得更加复杂，并可能导致单线程代码运行更慢。他进一步询问GIL移除后是否需要对多线程代码进行重构，例如增加锁。
• pjplp提到微软解散了加速Python团队，并质疑如果没有公司赞助，CPython的性能改进是否能持续。同时指出Facebook可能仍在赞助部分相关工作。
• heybrendan作为Python用户，询问`concurrent.futures`用户在GIL移除后会受到什么影响，以及需要做哪些改变。
• AlexanderDhoore表达了对GIL移除的担忧，认为复杂的多线程代码难以信任，尤其是动态语言如Python。
• make3强烈反对那些认为不使用线程更好的观点，认为多进程编程在实际应用中存在诸多限制，如对象序列化、fork在云环境中的不适用以及spawn的缓慢等问题，强调使用共享内存的线程会更高效和直接。
• YouWhy以20年Python开发经验为基础，认为多线程只对少数特定场景有用，且Python生态系统已有丰富的解决方案。此外，他提到像PyPy和numba等工具可以提供更高的性能，并鼓励大家了解和使用异步编程。

补充讨论：
• 0x000xca0xfe和amelius对页面头图中的双尾蛇提出调侃和疑问。
• aitchnyu询问当前除了库支持外，还有什么阻碍在单进程中启动WSGI和Celery worker。
• pawanjswal对Python性能改进的未来表示乐观。
• p0w3n3d用幽默的方式提到“小心后面的自由线程Python”。

争议焦点：
• GIL移除对多线程代码的影响及其必要性。
• 多进程与多线程编程在实际应用中的优劣对比，尤其是在性能和复杂性方面。

总结：评论中对GIL移除的潜在影响存在不同看法，部分人担心多线程代码的复杂性，而另一些人则认为多进程编程存在诸多限制，期待共享内存和多线程的优化方案。同时，也有对Python性能改进未来的期待和质疑。

Back to blog
The first year of free-threaded Python
Published
May 13, 2025
ngoldbaum
Nathan Goldbaum
Last week, the CPython developers rolled out CPython 3.14.0b1. This week, PyCon
2025 kicks off in Pittsburgh, PA. Both events mark a significant milestone for
the effort to ship and stabilize free-threaded Python.
This is the story of the first year of that effort and how our team at
Quansight played a key role in enabling experimental use of the free-threaded
build with real production workflows that depend on a complex set of
dependencies.
Introduction: Why are we working on community support for free-threaded Python?
Support for free-threaded Python unlocks the full compute power of modern
hardware with multicore CPUs and GPUs now commonplace. In the GIL-enabled
build, making full use of parallel algorithms that exploit all available
compute resources in Python requires workarounds and careful tuning. The Python
threading
module is often not used because the GIL prevents useful parallel
scaling. Instead, many reach for
multiprocessing
, but spawning processes is
expensive and communicating across processes often requires making expensive
copies of data that would not be necessary in a multithreaded program where
data is implicitly shared between threads.
Having said that, it is not possible for packages that ship compiled code in
their release distributions to support the free-threaded build out of the box.
Any package shipping native code (many Python packages do that) need to be
audited to ensure the package builds and does not suffer thread-safety issues
that are impossible on the GIL-enabled build.
Disabling the GIL required deep structural changes to the CPython
interpreter. Fully supporting the free-threaded build in existing packages
similarly requires fixing structural issues that until now were not big
problems. Things like use of global state in the implementation of a C extension
for convenience or for performance are no longer safe, since the GIL does not
protect simultaneous access from Python to the global state, allowing undefined
behavior via data races. While it is possible to trigger thread safety issues
like this using the
threading
module even with the GIL, most of the time the
GIL prevented these issues from surfacing. The free-threaded build makes fixing
these issues much more pressing.
Major accomplishments
Alongside the Python runtime team at Meta, we made significant contributions to
enable support for free-threaded Python in a long list of packages and
projects, including:
Packaging and project workflow tools like meson, meson-python, the
setup-python GitHub Actions workflow, packaging, pip, and setuptools.
Bindings generators like Cython, pybind11, f2py, and PyO3.
Foundational packages in the PyData ecosystem like NumPy, SciPy, PyArrow,
Matplotlib, pandas, scikit-learn, and scikit-image.
Top dependencies by PyPI downloads like Pillow, PyYAML, yarl, multidict,
and frozenlist.
We are also currently looking at popular packages that don't yet ship support,
including CFFI, cryptography, PyNaCl, aiohttp, SQLAlchemy, and grpcio as well
as popular libraries for machine learning workflows like safetensors and
tokenizers.
CPython core developers on our team also contributed several major improvements
that will ship in CPython 3.14:
The Python
warnings
module is now thread-safe by default on the
free-threaded build. It can be made thread-safe on the GIL-enabled build
with a configuration option or runtime command-line flag.
Significant thread safety issues in
asyncio
have been fixed. Our
benchmarks indicate substantially improved parallel scaling of code using
asyncio with a thread pool runner.
Thread safety overhaul in the
ctypes
module.
Substantial performance improvements for the free-threaded garbage collector.
Helped implement the deferred reference counting scheme used by the
free-threaded interpreter in 3.14.
Implemented several specializations for the adaptive specializing
interpreter and supported shipping optimizations that bring the
single-threaded performance of free-threaded CPython 3.14 within spitting
distance of the GIL-enabled build.
A huge number of smaller bugfixes and thread safety improvements.
We've also written a
comprehensive guide
for supporting free-threaded Python in existing apps and packages gleaned from
our experiences. Our hope is that the documentation we've written can be a
valuable resource for the "long tail" of packages that people will want to
update to support free-threaded Python in the coming years.
You can also read more about this effort from the team at Meta on the
Meta engineering blog
.
What is the state of the free-threaded Python ecosystem?
At this time last year, when Python 3.13.0b1 shipped, the wider ecosystem of
Python packages was more or less completely broken on the free-threaded build.

Quansight团队在多个方面做出了贡献，包括打包工具、绑定生成器、PyData生态系统的基础包及热门依赖包的支持。CPython核心开发者也进行了多项改进，如使warnings模块在无GIL构建中默认线程安全，修复asyncio和ctypes模块中的线程安全问题，以及提升垃圾回收器的性能。

一年前，Python包生态系统在无GIL构建中几乎完全无法运行，但现在情况已显著改善。本文还提到正在努力支持的其他流行包，并提供了一份详细指南以帮助其他开发者更新他们的包以支持无GIL的Python。

data.title: Beyond Text: On-Demand UI Generation for Better Conversational Experiences
data.author: fka
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了如何通过AI动态生成用户界面组件来改善人与AI的交互体验，解决纯文本交互的局限性。纯文本交互存在认知过载、歧义、输入验证困难、可访问性差、效率低和可视化限制等问题。作者提出了一种新原型，使大型语言模型（LLM）能够根据对话上下文按需生成动态、交互式的UI组件。例如，在客户支持场景中，AI可以生成完整的地址表单，而无需通过繁琐的文本问答。该方法通过自然语言请求、意图识别、组件生成和交互处理等步骤实现，并可与MCP服务无缝集成，提供标准化通信、降低认知负荷、增强功能和确保数据验证等优势。这种方法结合了对话AI的灵活性和传统应用界面的精确性与效率。

Beyond Text-Only AI: On-Demand UI Generation for Better Conversational Experiences
Open LLM-readable version of this post
Explore how AI-generated user interfaces can enhance human-AI interaction by dynamically creating the right interface components at the right time, addressing key limitations of text-only interactions.
Fatih Kadir Akın
In today’s AI-driven world, we’re increasingly interacting with sophisticated language models through simple text interfaces. While powerful, this raw text communication paradigm introduces significant user experience challenges that limit accessibility, efficiency, and ultimately user satisfaction.
What if AI systems could generate precisely the right interface components when needed, without requiring developers to build every possible UI variation in advance? This post explores my work on a new prototype that enables LLMs to create dynamic, interactive UI components on demand, transforming how users interact with AI systems and MCP servers.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Video demonstration of a shipping company support dialogue with AI-generated UI components
The Problem with Raw Text Interactions
Text-based interactions with AI have several inherent limitations:
Cognitive overload
: Users must translate their structured needs into unstructured text
Ambiguity
: Natural language is inherently ambiguous and prone to misinterpretation
Input validation
: No guardrails for ensuring correct data formats or required fields
Accessibility barriers
: Text-only interfaces exclude or complicate use for certain disabilities
Efficiency bottlenecks
: Typing complex instructions is slow and error-prone
Context management
: Text threads quickly become unwieldy for complex tasks
Visualization limitations
: Some information is best understood visually, not textually
For enterprise applications, customer service scenarios, and complex workflows, these limitations become even more pronounced. Consider a shipping company’s customer support system—asking users to provide complex shipping details, tracking numbers, or address information through pure text is frustratingly inefficient.
The Promise of AI-Generated UI Components
The solution lies in enabling AI to dynamically generate appropriate UI components based on the conversation context. When a shipping company customer needs to change their delivery address, instead of a cumbersome text exchange:
Bot: What's your new address?
User: 123 Main Street
Bot: What city?
User: New York
Bot: What's the ZIP code?
User: 10001
Bot: What state?
User: NY
The AI can generate a complete address form that collects all required fields at once, validates the input, and provides appropriate feedback—all while maintaining the conversational nature of the interaction.
This approach bridges the gap between conversational AI and traditional application interfaces, giving users the best of both worlds: the flexibility and naturalness of conversation with the precision and efficiency of structured inputs.
How LLM-UI Generation Works
The mechanism for generating UIs from LLMs follows this general pattern:
Request interpretation
: User makes a request through natural language
Intent recognition
: LLM identifies the task and required data points
Component selection
: LLM determines appropriate UI component(s) for the task
Component generation
: LLM generates structured JSON defining the UI component
Rendering
: Application renders the component alongside conversational response
Interaction handling
: User interacts with the component; data is collected
Structured processing
: The collected structured data is processed by the AI or backend system
From a technical standpoint, the LLM generates a JSON specification that describes the desired UI component, which the client application then renders using its component library.
Integration with MCP
The AI-generated UI approach pairs exceptionally well with MCP services. As discussed in my
previous post about MCP tools
, MCP provides standardized methods for communicating with MCPs. By extending MCP servers to accept structured data from UI components, we create a powerful ecosystem for human-AI interaction.
This integration offers several benefits:
Standardized communication
: UI components provide a consistent way to collect and validate inputs for MCP services
Reduced cognitive load
: Users interact with familiar interface patterns rather than learning service-specific text commands
Enhanced capabilities
: Complex MCP services become more accessible through purpose-built interfaces
Data validation
: Input validation happens at the UI level before data reaches MCP services
Seamless experience
: Users don’t need to understand the underlying MCP architecture

data.title: Ollama violating llama.cpp license for over a year
data.author: Jabrov
data.article_summary: 本文主要讨论了一个开源项目 **ollama** 中的许可证问题。具体而言，ollama 使用了 **llama.cpp** 作为静态链接依赖项，而根据 MIT 许可证的要求，应该在发布时包含版权声明。然而，用户在安装目录中未能找到相关版权声明，这违反了许可证规定。提交者建议至少应在二进制文件中包含版权声明，尽管有些人认为 README 文件中也应提及。当前问题被标记为一个 bug，需要修复。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源项目Ollama及其相关项目在MIT许可证下的版权声明和归属问题。

不同观点：
• rlpbb的观点：认为问题提交者提出的许可证问题不成立。他指出MIT许可证并未要求在二进制文件中包含版权声明，且在Debian等注重许可证合规的生态系统中，修补上游以在二进制文件中包含版权声明并非惯例。
• levifig的观点：指出llama.cpp与Ollama项目之间存在共生关系，问题提交者是在为他人感到不满，实际上已经有对源材料的认可。
• Havoc的观点：认为Ollama在增加易用性方面做出了贡献，只需对llama团队给予适当的明确认可即可解决问题，而非引发负面公众关系。
• Koshima的观点：认为推动明确的归属是合理的，但MIT许可证本身是宽松的，旨在简化代码共享。透明的 acknowledgment 可以避免很多矛盾。
• mkesper的观点：通过提供另一个项目的例子，认为Ollama应改进其acknowledgements并更彻底地检查许可证合规性。
• gittubaba的观点：质疑是否许多项目在二进制发布中包含完整的许可证文件，认为如果严格检查，很多流行工具可能都不合规。
• paxybs的观点：进一步解释MIT许可证的条款，认为Ollama的README中已经包含了对llama.cpp项目的链接，满足了许可证的要求。
• gmm1990的观点：指出Ollama和llama.cpp项目使用相同的MIT许可证，认为这已经足够。
• jjoergensen的观点：提到Ollama博客中对llama.cpp团队的感谢，认为这也是一种认可。
• aspenmayer的观点：通过类比HN指南，指出某些规则可能未在显眼位置说明，但仍然是有效的，这取决于如何传达信息。
• animitronix的观点：认为对开源许可证文件的抱怨是琐碎的，不关心这类问题。
• bethekidyouwant的观点：认为Ollama已经使用了MIT许可证，无需再抱怨，只需提交一个简单的合并请求即可解决问题。
• immibis的观点：认为只有当涉及诉讼时许可证问题才重要，通常公司知道哪些开源许可证可以忽略，例如SimpleX Chat项目。
• alfiedotwtf的观点：对长达一年的抱怨却无人提交PR（Pull Request）表示不解，认为直接实施更改会更有效。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于MIT许可证是否要求在二进制文件中包含版权声明，以及在实际项目中如何合理地满足这些要求。
• 讨论中涉及了开源社区中许可证合规性的实际操作和普遍做法，以及对版权声明和归属的合理认可方式。
• 部分评论者认为通过透明和适当的acknowledgment可以解决归属问题，避免负面公众关系。

ollama uses projects like llama.cpp as a statically linked dependency. The terms of the MIT license require that it distribute the copyright notice in both source and binary form. Yet if I
grep

• Koshima的观点：认为推动明确的归属是合理的，但MIT许可证本身是宽松的，旨在简化代码共享。透明的 acknowledgment 可以避免很多矛盾。
• mkesper的观点：通过提供另一个项目的例子，认为Ollama应改进其acknowledgements并更彻底地检查许可证合规性。
• gittubaba的观点：质疑是否许多项目在二进制发布中包含完整的许可证文件，认为如果严格检查，很多流行工具可能都不合规。
• paxybs的观点：进一步解释MIT许可证的条款，认为Ollama的README中已经包含了对llama.cpp项目的链接，满足了许可证的要求。
• gmm1990的观点：指出Ollama和llama.cpp项目使用相同的MIT许可证，认为这已经足够。
• jjoergensen的观点：提到Ollama博客中对llama.cpp团队的感谢，认为这也是一种认可。
• aspenmayer的观点：通过类比HN指南，指出某些规则可能未在显眼位置说明，但仍然是有效的，这取决于如何传达信息。
• animitronix的观点：认为对开源许可证文件的抱怨是琐碎的，不关心这类问题。
• bethekidyouwant的观点：认为Ollama已经使用了MIT许可证，无需再抱怨，只需提交一个简单的合并请求即可解决问题。
• immibis的观点：认为只有当涉及诉讼时许可证问题才重要，通常公司知道哪些开源许可证可以忽略，例如SimpleX Chat项目。
• alfiedotwtf的观点：对长达一年的抱怨却无人提交PR（Pull Request）表示不解，认为直接实施更改会更有效。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于MIT许可证是否要求在二进制文件中包含版权声明，以及在实际项目中如何合理地满足这些要求。
• 讨论中涉及了开源社区中许可证合规性的实际操作和普遍做法，以及对版权声明和归属的合理认可方式。
• 部分评论者认为通过透明和适当的acknowledgment可以解决归属问题，避免负面公众关系。

data.author: Towaway69
data.article_summary: Erlang-RED 是一个基于 Erlang 的可视化低代码编程环境，旨在替代 Node-RED 的 NodeJS 后端，实现与其流程代码的 100% 兼容（JavaScript 功能节点除外）。该项目利用 Erlang 的天然并发和消息传递优势，提升 Node-RED 的性能和并发处理能力。开发过程采用基于测试流的开发策略，通过一组测试流确保节点功能与 Node-RED 匹配。当前支持部分节点和功能，如 `catch`、`change`、`debug`、`delay`、`exec`、`function` 等，但一些复杂功能如动态延迟、多输出端口、JSONata 高级功能等尚未支持。项目架构体现了节点间的紧密联系，以确保正确的节点交互和异常处理。

Erlang-RED - A Node-RED backend coded in Erlang
An experiment to replace Node-REDs existing NodeJS backend with an Erlang equivalent that is 100% compatible[1] to existing flow code.
The goal is bring the advantages of low-code visual flow-based programming to a programming language that is designed for message passing and concurrency from the ground up, hence Erlang.
[1] = 100% won't be possible since function nodes that are coded in Javascript aren't supported (or aren't intended to be supported - unless someone has a workaround)
Why?
Node-RED
is a amazing[*] tool for creating flows that describe concurrent processing, it is just a shame the NodeJS is single threaded. So why not use something that is multi-process from the ground up? Concurrency is guaranteed and included.
Also Erlang isn't the most understandable of programming language - unless one has fallen into in a
cauldron
of Prolog, spiced with Lisp.
So won't it be great to have the simplicity of low-code visual flow based programming and the performance (and concurrency) of Erlang?
[*] = amazing in the sense of
extendability
(Nodes can easily be added and developed by third parties),
understandability
(Node-RED
terminology
is straightforward) and
usability
(once a rectangle becomes a unit of computation and a line becomes a pathway for data flow)
Development Strategy
My development process is best described as
flow driven development
based around a set of
test flows
to ensure that node functionality is implemented correctly - meaning that it matches the existing Node-RED functionality.
Test flows are mirrored in a separate
repository
for better maintainability and also integration with existing Node-RED installations.
Architecture
The architecture, along with a background to Flow Based Programming and Node-RED has been
written
.
The codebase as it stands, has many interdependence because of testing flows:
assert nodes
need to know about
web-socket communication
, or because of the nature of nodes: the
complete
node needs to know of
completed messages
.
While the
exception node
needs to know about exceptions when they
happen
.
An architectural diagram of this interconnectedness would be probably be just as confusing as the code itself.

data.title: Show HN: SQL-tString a t-string SQL builder in Python
data.author: pgjones
data.article_summary: SQL-tString 是一个用于构建 SQL 查询的 Python 库，类似于 f-string，但能防止 SQL 注入。它通过 `t-strings` 来插入变量，并将这些变量转换为 SQL 占位符，同时支持预定义的表和列名。使用 `sql_context` 可以限制允许的列和表名，防止注入攻击。如果变量设为 `Absent`，库会自动移除相关参数，适用于可选更新或条件语句。此外，还支持 `IsNull` 和 `IsNotNull` 来处理 SQL 中的 `NULL` 条件。默认使用 `qmark` 参数样式，但也支持其他如 `asyncpg` 样式。对于 Python 3.12 和 3.13，可通过 `locals()` 使用该库。该项目基于 MIT 许可证，目前有 43 个星标。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：T-SQL字符串模板的使用及其相关功能和安全性

不同观点：
• throwaway127482认为，对于不同部分的查询需要不同的列集，当前设计可能需要提供子查询中所有支持的列的超集，这看起来有些危险。
• hombre_fatal赞赏该功能，认为它可以避免传统方式中通过多个if语句构建where子句的复杂性，使得查询语句更直观，减少调试困难。
• bvrman（sqlbind的作者）指出，简单查询可以通过其他方式编写，但动态查询（根据条件删除部分查询）是一个真正的问题，并认为该解决方案非常巧妙。
• schultzer关注SQL解析器的实现，建议基于BNF语法构建词法分析器和解析器，并进行一致性测试。
• caturopath解释了`sql_context(columns="x")`的用法，并指出columns是一个字符串集合，可能导致误解。
• jitl关心SQL重写的机制，尤其在处理非标准SQL功能和复杂查询时，同时询问是否支持模板嵌套。
• badmonster询问如何在不使用手动字符串拼接的情况下，安全地组合查询片段，特别是条件构建WHERE子句或JOIN。
• ilyagr建议允许类似Rust的`format!`功能，通过`sql(t"SELECT {}", a - 1)`实现动态SQL构建。
• bencyoung认为Absent功能可能导致误删WHERE子句，造成潜在危险。
• sirfz指出T-SQL字符串强化了参数化查询，并可能用于构建统一的SQL客户端接口。
• owlstuffing提倡语言应内置类型安全的SQL操作，提到Java通过Manifold项目实现这一目标。
• 90s_dev赞赏该库但批评了使用词法作用域进行占位符查找的设计，认为应通过显式字典传递参数。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Absent功能的安全性，部分用户担心误删重要查询部分。
• 另一个焦点是T-SQL字符串中占位符的处理方式，部分用户认为词法作用域设计不理想，建议使用显式字典传递参数。
• 用户对SQL重写和动态查询构建的功能表示关注，尤其是处理复杂查询时的安全性和可控性。
• 不同用户对T-SQL字符串模板的功能有不同的期待，包括对简单查询和复杂查询的支持程度。

SQL-tString
SQL-tString allows for t-string based construction of sql queries
without allowing for SQL injection. The basic usage is as follows,
from
sql_tstring
import
sql
a
=
1
query
,
values
=
sql
(
t
"""SELECT a, b, c
FROM tbl
WHERE a = {a}"""
,
)
The
query
is a
str
and
values
a
list[Any]
, both are
then typically passed to a DB connection. Note the parameters can only
be identifiers that identify variables (in the above example in the
locals()) e.g.
{a - 1}
is not valid.
SQL-tString will convert parameters to SQL placeholders where
appropriate. In other locations SQL-tString will allow pre defined
column or table names to be used,
from
sql_tstring
import
sql
,
sql_context
col
=
"a"
table
=
"tbl"
with
sql_context
(
columns
=
{
"a"
},
tables
=
{
"tbl"
}):
query
,
values
=
sql
(
t
"SELECT {col} FROM {table}"
,
)
If the value of
col
or
table
does not match the valid values
given to the
sql_context
function an error will be raised.
Rewriting values
SQL-tString will also remove parameters if they are set to the special
value of
Absent
(or
RewritingValue.Absent
). This is most
useful for optional updates, or conditionals,
from
sql_tstring
import
Absent
,
sql
a
=
Absent
b
=
Absent
query
,
values
=
sql
(
t
"""UPDATE tbl
SET a = {a},
b = 1
WHERE b = {b}"""
,
)
As both
a
and
b
are
Absent
the above
query
will be
UPDATE tbl SET b =1
.
In addition for conditionals the values
IsNull
(or
RewritingValue.IS_NULL
) and
IsNotNull
(or
RewritingValue.IS_NOT_NULL
) can be used to rewrite the conditional
as expected. This is useful as
x = NULL
is always false in SQL.
Paramstyle (dialect)
By default SQL-tString uses the
qmark
paramstyle
(dialect) but also
supports the
$
paramstyle or asyncpg dialect. This is best changed
globally via,
from
sql_tstring
import
Context
,
set_context
set_context
(
Context
(
dialect
=
"asyncpg"
))
Pre Python 3.14 usage
t-strings were introduced in Python 3.14 via,
PEP 750
, however this library can be
used with Python 3.12 and 3.13 as follows,
from
sql_tstring
import
sql
a
=
1
query
,
values
=
sql
(
"""SELECT a, b, c
FROM tbl
WHERE a = {a}"""
,
locals
(),
)
Please note though that only simple variable identifiers can be placed
within the braces.

• bvrman（sqlbind的作者）指出，简单查询可以通过其他方式编写，但动态查询（根据条件删除部分查询）是一个真正的问题，并认为该解决方案非常巧妙。
• schultzer关注SQL解析器的实现，建议基于BNF语法构建词法分析器和解析器，并进行一致性测试。
• caturopath解释了`sql_context(columns="x")`的用法，并指出columns是一个字符串集合，可能导致误解。
• jitl关心SQL重写的机制，尤其在处理非标准SQL功能和复杂查询时，同时询问是否支持模板嵌套。
• badmonster询问如何在不使用手动字符串拼接的情况下，安全地组合查询片段，特别是条件构建WHERE子句或JOIN。
• ilyagr建议允许类似Rust的`format!`功能，通过`sql(t"SELECT {}", a - 1)`实现动态SQL构建。
• bencyoung认为Absent功能可能导致误删WHERE子句，造成潜在危险。
• sirfz指出T-SQL字符串强化了参数化查询，并可能用于构建统一的SQL客户端接口。
• owlstuffing提倡语言应内置类型安全的SQL操作，提到Java通过Manifold项目实现这一目标。
• 90s_dev赞赏该库但批评了使用词法作用域进行占位符查找的设计，认为应通过显式字典传递参数。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Absent功能的安全性，部分用户担心误删重要查询部分。
• 另一个焦点是T-SQL字符串中占位符的处理方式，部分用户认为词法作用域设计不理想，建议使用显式字典传递参数。
• 用户对SQL重写和动态查询构建的功能表示关注，尤其是处理复杂查询时的安全性和可控性。
• 不同用户对T-SQL字符串模板的功能有不同的期待，包括对简单查询和复杂查询的支持程度。

data.title: Sci-Net
data.author: greyface-
data.article_summary:
Sci-Net是一个新的社交网络平台，旨在请求和分享科研文章。由于Sci-Hub数据库更新暂停，请求获取无法通过Sci-Hub下载的论文的需求增加。Sci-Net允许用户请求未提供的论文，并上传他们拥有的论文，平台还具备自动去除PDF水印的功能以保护上传者匿名性。用户可以通过DOI请求和上传文章，上传的论文对所有用户免费开放。

Sci-Net的独特之处在于使用去中心化代币——Sci-Hub代币，以奖励知识分享。请求者可以为上传者设定奖励代币，上传完成并确认后才转移代币。注册需要至少1000个Sci-Hub代币，这笔象征性费用用于奖励上传者，而非平台。与传统出版商付费墙不同，Sci-Net的文章一旦上传即永久免费。Sci-Hub代币的价值随使用人数增加而提升，间接支持Sci-Hub的维护和发展。尽管获取代币可能对新手有一定挑战，但这增加了过程的趣味性。

Sci-Net旨在实现开放知识理念，研究者应积极参与贡献。

◻ ◻ ◻ ◻ ◻ ◻
Sci-Net
A new social network platform to request and share research articles
I regularly receive requests from Sci-Hub users to help them download some paper that cannot be opened through Sci-Hub. The number of such requests increased in the past two years, since Sci-Hub database updates were paused. The opposite also happens: users ask whether they can upload to Sci-Hub some paper that they have bought or downloaded via university subscription.
Sci-Hub was never designed to accept uploads from users. From the very beginning, it was implemented as an autonomous system that scans and downloads research papers from various universities ‐ without human in the loop. This automatic method turned out to be quite effective, and Sci-Hub was able to reach coverage > 90% in its best days. However, even then some paper remained unreachable.
Now there exists a platform where users can request unavailable papers, and upload them:
sci-net.xyz
Introducing Sci-Net
The user interface is simple: an input box where a DOI of the requested paper should be inserted. Once the user clicks the button, Sci-Net automatically checks if the requested paper is open access or already available on Sci-Hub. If the paper is found, the link to it will be displayed. If not, then user will be able to create a new request.
On the index page, the list of requests is shown, that can be filtered by subjects and publisher. If you happen to have access to some paper in the list, you can click on the request and upload the PDF. There is a nice built-in functionality to remove watermarks from PDF to hide the university where paper was downloaded. That way Sci-Net protects the anonymity of the uploader.
The 'Library' section will show all your requests and uploads, and in the 'Upload' section you can contribute your papers to the platform: just drop the PDF file and the system will automatically detect the DOI. If the DOI is not available yet on Sci-Net / Sci-Hub / open access, the file will get uploaded. The article then will become accessible to everyone by URL sci-net.xyz/DOI including people who are not registered on the platform.
The platform is currently in the active development stage, and much more features are upcoming.
Sci-Net tokenomics
The part that really makes Sci-Net stand out is the usage of decentralized tokens: Sci-Hub meme coins -- to reward knowledge sharing. When creating a request, you can specify the amount of tokens uploader will receive for sharing the paper. However, the tokens will not be transferred after uploading the PDF right away, but only after you check the solution and click the 'Accept' button. The tokens subtracted from your account will be added to the uploader.
Sci-Net will ask for a minimum amount of 1000 Sci-Hub tokens to register. The tokens will appear on your account after registration and will be used to reward uploaders. That is the most controversial part: some people argue that Sci-Net introduces paywall similar to publisher.
Even though both might appear similar at a first glance, the differences are profound. Compared to insane publisher paywalls, the entry tax on Sci-Net is symbolic and is not higher than an equivalent of a cup of coffee in most countries. The next difference is that in traditional approach, profits are made by publisher, and ordinary researcher has no control on how the money are used. On Sci-Net, you're using tokens directly to reward uploaders. Payments go to fellow researchers, not to the platform.
But the most important is that publishers will charge for access to the same paper again and again. Sci-Net will only do that once when paper is uploaded and after that, it will remain free forever and for everyone -- even users who are not registered on the platform will be able to access it. That is, all Sci-Net transactions contribute directly to public domain, and the number of knowledge accessible to everyone grows with Sci-Net usage.
The more people use Sci-Hub token, the more valuable it becomes. That way Sci-Net indirectly contributes to maintenance and further development of Sci-Hub.
The only downside is that obtaining Sci-Hub tokens on the Solana network can be a non-trivial puzzle for a user who are new to crypto. But that only makes the process more interesting.
Conclusion
Overall, Sci-Net is a platform that every researcher today must use and contribute to -- together, we can gradually make the idea of open knowledge a reality.

data.title: Tower Defense: Cache Control
data.author: jasonthorsness
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了网页缓存技术，以帮助在小预算下应对大量网络流量。作者以自己网站为例，介绍了不同难度级别的缓存策略：

1. **简单级别**： mostly-static sites（ mostly-静态网站），如个人博客。使用内容哈希资源（content-hashed resources）和CDN（内容分发网络）缓存静态内容，确保长时间缓存且无需频繁更新。
   
2. **中等级别**： data-driven dynamic sites（数据驱动的动态网站）。通过将动态部分放在客户端，并利用CDN和Etag头来减少服务器负载和数据传输。

3. **困难级别**： authenticated per-user sites（每用户认证的网站），涉及更复杂的个性化内容处理。

作者详细介绍了如何通过内容哈希和CDN来提高网站性能，减少请求和响应时间，最终实现高效的缓存策略。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕缓存策略、CDN选择及其实现复杂性的技术讨论

不同观点：
• **grep_it** 支持使用Redis作为缓存方案，认为Redis内存占用低且易于运行，尤其在单服务器上有很好的表现。相比SQLite，Redis可以有效缓存API请求，且资源消耗不大。

• **kawsper** 指出"stale-while-revalidate"缓存控制选项早在2015年Varnish 4.1版本中就已支持，反驳这种策略是新概念的说法。给出了具体版本更新文档作为论据，强调Varnish对此功能的长久支持。

• **harrall** 强调在处理大规模请求时，CDN的请求合并能力至关重要，并以自己处理超过350,000请求/秒的经验为例，建议仔细阅读CDN文档，确保其具备处理高并发请求的能力。

• **ec109685** 对"stale-while-revalidate"策略提出潜在问题，认为如果响应时间超过15秒或出现服务器错误（如500错误），可能导致缓存失效或系统过载。强调需要为错误情况配置缓存策略以防止系统崩溃。

• **tikotus** 描述了自己在使用CDN和静态内容托管时遇到的困难，尤其是针对低流量服务但在可能爆发流量时需要扩展的场景。对DigitalOcean的各种解决方案（如Spaces、App Platform、Docker Registry）的适用性提出质疑，并表达了对DDoS防护和缓存机制的担忧。

• **arjie** 分享了自己使用Cloudflare为非登录用户缓存博客内容的体验，认为Cloudflare提供了很好的缓存控制，尤其是在使用Mediawiki这样可能变慢的应用时，显著提升了用户访问速度。

• **nixpulvis** 提出是否值得告知用户他们的请求是陈旧的，并建议探讨现代缓存架构如何处理用户刷新需求的问题。对缓存刷新机制和用户体验之间的关系表示关注。

补充讨论：
• **nisten** 并未参与技术讨论，而是表达了对文中提到的潜在游戏的兴趣。

争议焦点：
• **缓存策略的可靠性**：ec109685对stale-while-revalidate策略在处理响应延迟和服务器错误时的潜在问题提出了质疑，而kawsper则强调该策略的成熟性和长期支持。

• **CDN和缓存方案的复杂性**：tikotus对选择合适的CDN和服务托管方案感到困惑，尤其是在考虑扩展性和DDoS防护时，对多种方案的适用性提出了疑问。

• **用户体验与缓存机制的结合**：nixpulvis对如何在用户体验和缓存刷新机制之间找到平衡表示关注，提出了是否应告知用户请求陈旧的问题。

整体来看，讨论围绕缓存策略、CDN选择及其实现复杂性展开，涵盖了技术方案的可靠性、适用性及用户体验等方面。

May 12 25
Tower Defense: Cache Control
26
—
May 12 25
share on
twitter icon
share on
twitter icon
For those of you who landed here directly and missed my
implausible intro
,
this isn’t a game. It’s something even better: an article about caching!
I’ll describe the techniques used on my sites
jasonthorsness.com
and
hn.unlurker.com
. The latter is open-source so you can
peruse the implementation
.
If you are looking to defend a meager budget with web-exposed side projects from an onslaught of web
traffic you might find these approaches helpful.
And if you are part of the problem, a user among countless others in your horde, driven en masse in
wave after wave against my defenses — read on to scout my setup and find out whether or not it’s up
to the challenge.
The article progresses through three difficulty levels:
Difficulty Level
Description
Easy
Mostly-static sites
Medium
Data-driven dynamic sites
Hard
Authenticated per-user sites
Easy: Mostly-Static Sites
Static means the content is the same for every user and doesn’t change as a function of time. For
example, due to my sluggish pace of writing,
jasonthorsness.com
remains unchanged for weeks in
between updates. Even then, my
older articles like this one
don’t change unless I adjust a
common layout. For this kind of site, applying content-hashed resources, using a CDN, and keeping
dynamic bits client-side is the dominant industry combination.
Content-Hashed Resources
To improve the handling of supporting resources (CSS, JS, images, etc.) a universal practice in
modern web frameworks is to add content hashes to the resource names. By deriving the name of the
file from its contents, you can consider a file with a given name unchanging. For example, on this
site, one of the fonts is at the time of writing served as
/_next/static/media/bd734242e06bd6ad-s.p.woff2
with the cache-control header of
public,max-age=31536000,immutable
. The
bd734242e06bd6ad
part of the name is a hash of the file
contents. The CDN and the user’s browser will cache this file for as long as they want without
worrying about it becoming stale. If I ever change the font, the file will have a different name so
all caches will miss and fetch the new font from the origin.
If you open the network tab in your browser’s dev tools and refresh this page, you’ll see most
resources are served in this manner and arrive in 0-1 ms from the memory or disk cache. This is
simultaneously the least costly and lowest-latency sort of caching — nothing does any work except
the user’s browser.
resources served from disk or memory
🏰 In Tower Defense lingo: content-hashed static files in the browser cache let you defeat waves of
requests right at the spawn point.
CDNs
Resources referenced from outside the site itself, like the path you see in the URL bar, can’t have
hashes appended because the links would be broken whenever the content changes. The server instead
delivers the response with an “Etag” header that identifies the current version of the content. When
the browser requests the resource again, it includes the last Etag value in an “If-None-Match”
header. Whenever the current ETag on the server matches the If-None-Match value from the browser,
the server is allowed to respond with
304 Not Modified
rather than the actual content.
If you open the network tab in your browser’s dev tools once more and refresh this page, you’ll see
/26
is served with a
304
response. You should also see fewer than 2 kiB transferred for the
entire page! If you see more than that, it’s likely browser extensions you have injecting stuff. Try
it again in Incognito Mode or with a guest profile.
A problem with
304 Not Modified
is that there’s still a round-trip to the server. But is it really
a problem? If you look carefully at that network tab, you might see
/26
served to you in fewer
than ~60 milliseconds. The single origin server for this page is somewhere in the eastern US, but
the reported latency will stay low worldwide. This is because rather than serving from the origin,
the resources are cached and served from a network of delivery points around the globe, commonly
described as a CDN (content-delivery network). This reduces load on the origin and ensures snappy
performance for users all over the world. Low-latency world-wide is important if you respect your
users — even this irrelevant blog regularly gets traffic from USA, Europe, and Asia.
This site uses Vercel’s CDN, which has at the time of this writing
119 locations
to serve content. Beyond static
resources, you can also run code in these locations to implement
custom low-latency functionality
.
low-latency, low-transfer
🏰 CDN locations are the towers in-between the spawn point and your base. When things are working
correctly they take care of most of the waves.
What About The Dynamic Parts?
Even a mostly-static site might have dynamic components. For example, beyond the
city search

43972449.article_summary:
本文讨论了网页缓存技术，以帮助在小预算下应对大量网络流量。作者以自己网站为例，介绍了不同难度级别的缓存策略：

1. **简单级别**： mostly-static sites（ mostly-静态网站），如个人博客。使用内容哈希资源（content-hashed resources）和CDN（内容分发网络）缓存静态内容，确保长时间缓存且无需频繁更新。
   
2. **中等级别**： data-driven dynamic sites（数据驱动的动态网站）。通过将动态部分放在客户端，并利用CDN和Etag头来减少服务器负载和数据传输。

3. **困难级别**： authenticated per-user sites（每用户认证的网站），涉及更复杂的个性化内容处理。

作者详细介绍了如何通过内容哈希和CDN来提高网站性能，减少请求和响应时间，最终实现高效的缓存策略。

data.article_summary:
文章探讨了英国皇家海军在风帆时代（1670-1827年）为何能够 dominance 海上，重点分析了制度激励的作用。作者援引道格拉斯·艾伦的观点，指出英国海军的成功并非源于技术优势，因为当时各国海军在装备和技术上差别不大。关键在于有效的激励机制和监督设计：

1. **补偿机制**：海军军官有丰厚的战利品分成，且不在海上执勤的军官只拿一半薪水，形成一种“效率工资”机制，促使军官积极参战。
2. **晋升制度**：与陆军不同，海军中的舰长按资历晋升，只要不丢脸，最终能成为舰队司令，激励他们勇敢作战。
3. **监督机制**：采用“战列线”战术，方便舰队司令监督各舰长的表现；同时，副官和船长日志相互独立，形成监督机制。

这些设计有效解决了海上监控困难、随机性强以及激励不匹配的问题，使英国海军在多次战争中取得显著优势。
